front_blocks.md: Define the term **malleable**.

back_blocks.md: A **malleable** material can be hammered or pressed into different shapes without breaking. Metals are malleable because layers of positive metal ions can slide over each other.

front_blocks.md: Why do metals conduct electricity?

back_blocks.md: Metals conduct electricity because they have **delocalised electrons** that are free to move through the metal structure, carrying charge.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Most non-metals have high melting and boiling points.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
Most **non-metals** have low melting and boiling points because they have weak intermolecular forces that require little energy to overcome. Many are gases at room temperature.

front_blocks.md: Define the term **ductile**.

back_blocks.md: A **ductile** material can be drawn out into wires without breaking. Metals are ductile because layers of positive metal ions can slide over each other.

front_blocks.md: What products form when a metal reacts with cold water?

back_blocks.md: When a metal reacts with cold water, the products are a **metal hydroxide** and **hydrogen** gas.
For example: Ca (s) + 2H<sub>2</sub>O (l) → Ca(OH)<sub>2</sub> (aq) + H<sub>2</sub> (g)

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
When a metal reacts with steam, the products are a metal hydroxide and hydrogen.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
When a metal reacts with **steam**, the products are a **metal oxide** and **hydrogen**. It is not a metal hydroxide. A metal hydroxide forms only when the metal reacts with cold water.

back_blocks.md: When a metal reacts with an acid, the **hydrogen** atom in the acid is replaced by the metal to produce a **salt** and hydrogen gas.

front_blocks.md: Why are non-metals described as brittle when solid?

back_blocks.md: Non-metals are **brittle** because, unlike metals, their electrons are all involved in covalent bonding. The layers cannot slide over each other, so the structure shatters when force is applied.

front_blocks.md: What property of **aluminium** makes it suitable for making aircraft bodies?

back_blocks.md: **Aluminium** has a **low density** (giving a high strength-to-weight ratio), which keeps aircraft lightweight without sacrificing strength.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
**Copper** is a better electrical conductor than aluminium. Aluminium is still chosen for overhead cables because of other properties that matter more for long suspended spans.

front_blocks.md: Why is aluminium resistant to corrosion despite being a reactive metal?

back_blocks.md: Aluminium forms a thin, protective layer of **aluminium oxide** on its surface. This layer prevents oxygen and water from reaching the metal underneath, stopping further corrosion.

front_blocks.md: Define the term **alloy**.

back_blocks.md: An **alloy** is a mixture of a metal with other elements. Most alloys contain more than one metal, but some contain non-metals.

front_blocks.md: What metals make up **brass**, and why is it useful?

back_blocks.md: **Brass** is an alloy of **copper** and **zinc**. It is much stronger than either pure metal, making it useful for musical instruments, ornaments, and door knobs.

front_blocks.md: Stainless steel is an alloy of **..........**  and other elements such as **..........**,  nickel and carbon. It is used in cutlery because of its hardness and resistance to rusting.

Alloys are compounds because they contain more than one element.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
**Alloys** are **mixtures**, not compounds. The elements in an alloy are not chemically combined, so the alloy does not have a fixed chemical formula.

front_blocks.md: How can you identify an alloy from a diagram of its structure?

back_blocks.md: An alloy is shown by a diagram with **different-sized particles** arranged in **irregular, distorted layers**. A pure metal has uniform-sized particles in regular rows.

back_blocks.md: Alloys contain atoms of **different sizes**, which distort the regular arrangement of layers. This makes it harder for the layers to **slide over each other**, so the alloy is harder and stronger.
